topics.label: Introduction and lecture course overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, student background contexts, and the session's core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Carcinogenesis as a failure of genetic regulation and tissue differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how the accumulation of genetic alterations disrupts normal developmental differentiation programs and tissue architecture to initiate tumor growth.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how neoplasms are evaluated histologically for invasiveness and how benign lesions can progress into metastatic disease.

topics.label: Neoplasm nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and exceptions used to name benign and malignant tumors according to their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the anatomical and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause debilitating illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across tissues and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of tumor prevalence, tissue susceptibility, and mortality across human populations and other multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Principles and clinical modalities of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the rationale, histological basis, and comparative efficacy of population screening programmes for early tumor detection.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with a recap of learning outcomes and practical course arrangements.
